transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia (Redwood); Arjun, Nina, Tom (HelixHealth)

Summary (auto): quick recap of experiment numbers, decision gate criteria, handoff tasks

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone, thanks for joining — we can start, we've got about 45 minutes on the agenda, first we'll run through the latest numbers then ops handoff.
[00:18] Nina Lopez: sounds good, quick note — sorry I'm juggling two screens, so if I freeze just ping me.
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: no worries, Nina. I'll start with the bench numbers, quick caveat some of the labels in the sheet are auto-exported so there might be mis-typed model ids.
[00:35] Liam O'Neill: (screen share) Alright, here's `quant-bench-v3.csv` — baseline fp16 on the left, int8 middle, fp8-right, and a blended profile we call int8-fp8-hybrid.
[00:50] Liam O'Neill: p50/p90/p95 token latencies: baseline p95 is ~180ms, INT8 bumped that to 210ms in worst-case long sequences, FP8 sits at 190ms. Throughput gains look like 1.9x for INT8 peak, FP8 about 1.6x.
[01:12] Tom Becker: so INT8 gives the most throughput, but latency tail gets worse — that's the feeling we had. Any idea why p95 goes up?
[01:22] Liam O'Neill: yeah, it's the mix of kernel fallbacks and KV cache alignment. For certain layers the quant kernels need an extra copy or a slower path on your current driver; that inflates the tail. We identified 3 transformer blocks where quantization heatmap showed higher flop variance.
[01:40] Arjun Patel: can you point to which blocks, Liam? We need to map that to our model shard placement.
[01:46] Liam O'Neill: sure, blocks 7-9 in the mid layers. We'll annotate the sheet with the layer-level diffs. There is also a note: on your A100 fleet the cuDNN/driver combo triggers a fallback at long sequences >1024.
[02:05] Maya Chen: quick business note — for this sprint our success gate was max 2% quality delta on the golden prompt set and p95 latency <= 1.1x baseline. Current INT8 is about 2.8% on exact-match quality and 1.16x p95, FP8 is 1.1% delta and 1.06x p95.
[02:30] Nina Lopez: so FP8 is within both thresholds but INT8 slightly over quality and latency, correct?
[02:35] Maya Chen: correct. INT8 gives a bigger cost win (~28% per-token), but we want to avoid QA-visible regressions.
[02:42] Nina Lopez: for HelixHealth, any hallucination uptick is non-starter, we have safety audits.
[02:49] Sofia Reyes: understood — we've been running an SNR analysis across your clinical QA prompts; INT8 showed a slight increase in confidence misalignment for named entities. FP8 didn't show that pattern.
[03:05] Arjun Patel: named entities are critical; can you share examples? We can test them in prod-like contexts.
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: yes, we'll export a short set of failing prompts and anonymize them; it's in the shared drive: https://redwood.internal/bench/ff-helix-quant/examples (placeholder)
[03:22] Tom Becker: on the infra side, if we pick FP8, what's the operational delta? Do we need kernel installs or special docker images?
[03:31] Sofia Reyes: FP8 path is relatively straightforward. There is a small runtime flag and the quantized weights. Most of the heavy lifting was done in the model compilation step. INT8 might need a micro-patch for your driver stack, so it's more ops work.
[03:45] Nina Lopez: curious — if we go FP8 in prod will we lose the option to go to INT8 later?
[03:50] Liam O'Neill: no, you can route by model variant. Redwood supports routing policies — can do canary traffic to an INT8 variant once we've got patches. We recommended a canary window plus automatic fallback to FP8 or FP16 if quality thresholds slip.
[04:05] Arjun Patel: about fallback — will the KV cache survive switching variants? We can't afford cold-cache penalties for each request.
[04:12] Liam O'Neill: good call — KV cache formats are compatible between these quant variants in our runtime if the model architecture and tokenization are identical. There are caveats for recompiled kernels; we have a cache versioning tag to avoid invalidation when a weight-format change occurs. We'll include that in the runbook.
[04:33] Maya Chen: let's pivot to the decision matrix — we proposed two tracks: immediate FP8 rollout for production with canary, or delayed INT8 after a small kernel patch and an ops window. Thoughts?
[04:45] Nina Lopez: FP8 first. Lower risk, meets criteria. We can chase INT8 for a cost delta if the ops patch is low-risk and timeboxed.
[04:53] Tom Becker: agree FP8 first, but show me the rollback playbook; also we need SSO/KMS notes because we're on a VPC and keys are in our HSM.
[05:03] Sofia Reyes: we'll add an HSM/KMS integration section. Redwood's Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and we have a SOC 2 + ISO note in the security pack. We'll send the security addendum link in the email.
[05:18] Arjun Patel: perfect. Are there any outstanding legal/compliance blockers we should flag before ops workshop?
[05:24] Maya Chen: none beyond the usual — data residency? you mentioned europe earlier.
[05:29] Nina Lopez: not for this pilot, but production must be us-east only. We'll note that in the runbook.
[05:34] Liam O'Neill: back to the numbers — we also tested mixed-precision routing where token-prefixes critical to retrieval run at FP16 while dense generation runs at FP8; that preserved named-entity fidelity in 87% of cases while keeping throughput higher than baseline. It's an interesting middle ground.
[05:55] Arjun Patel: mixed routing sounds promising but sounds complex to implement on our side. How invasive is the code change?
[06:01] Sofia Reyes: it's largely a config-level change if you use our SDK/route hooks. If you have bespoke orchestration, Liam and I can work with Tom to add the routing hook; it's about 3-4 PRs on the orchestration and small changes to request headers.
[06:20] Tom Becker: 3-4 PRs is fine as long as the runtime switch doesn't break A/B analysis.
[06:25] Liam O'Neill: we'll make the header idempotent and add trace tags so A/B persists.
[06:30] Nina Lopez: can we talk about the golden prompt set? we saw you used 500 prompts — is that a production-reflective sample?
[06:37] Liam O'Neill: it's a curated 500, heavy on clinical Q&A and entity extraction, plus 50 adversarial edge cases. We can expand it if you'd like more coverage.
[06:45] Nina Lopez: expand to 800 with more long form docs please. Also include confidence scoring probes.
[06:51] Maya Chen: noted — action item for Helix to validate. Arjun?
[06:55] Arjun Patel: will do, we'll provide the extended set by 6/20.
[07:01] Maya Chen: okay, next — risk register. Liam?
[07:05] Liam O'Neill: top risks: 1) INT8 p95 tail regressions tied to driver fallback; 2) entity hallucination increase in certain prompts; 3) KV cache invalidation in the event of recompile. Mitigations: more aggressive canary, fallbacks, runbook with cache versioning, and targeted kernel patch for driver.
[07:26] Tom Becker: for the kernel patch, who owns testing? Our infra or Redwood?
[07:31] Sofia Reyes: Redwood will provide patch and unit/integration tests; Helix will run smoke in their staging and Redwood will support across the window. We'll document the exact steps.
[07:43] Nina Lopez: what's the expected ops downtime for the patch?
[07:47] Liam O'Neill: patch can be hot if it's a user-space driver layer replacement, but worst-case a rolling restart per node — approximately 5-8 minutes per node if validation included. We'll quantify after profiling your fleet.
[07:59] Arjun Patel: we have 12 nodes in the A100 cluster, rolling restart at 8 minutes each is disruptive. Need a scheduled maintenance window.
[08:08] Maya Chen: agreed, that's why FP8 first avoids that need; INT8 can be scheduled in a quieter maintenance window.
[08:15] Nina Lopez: timeline? if we choose FP8 this week, how soon can we be live?
[08:20] Sofia Reyes: assuming Helix runs the golden set and we sign off, we can do a canary next week and production in 2 weeks. So potentially 2026-07-01 for small-scale prod.
[08:32] Arjun Patel: ok that fits our internal target (end of July).
[08:36] Maya Chen: I'll send a proposed timeline in follow-up.
[08:40] Liam O'Neill: quick note on monitoring — we suggest custom eval hooks: per-prompt QA checks, SNR tracking, and latency spike alerting at 95th. We'll add recommended thresholds in the runbook.
[08:54] Nina Lopez: send that as well.
[08:57] Tom Becker: two small asks: 1) sample runbook for fallback logic (we need actual curl examples), 2) KMS/HSM integration checklist.
[09:05] Maya Chen: got it — action items captured.
[09:09] Sofia Reyes: one more technical point — runtime handles mixed-precision blending at token granularity but there's a small overhead for switching precision within a single generation; in our tests overhead was ~6-8% throughput cost but recovered quality for named entities. So it's a trade.
[09:28] Arjun Patel: can we get a small POC for token-granularity blending on a couple of endpoints?
[09:33] Liam O'Neill: yes, we'll prepare a blending POC config.
[09:37] Nina Lopez: final question: pricing impact if we go FP8 vs INT8?
[09:42] Maya Chen: FP8 is about 18% token cost reduction vs baseline; INT8 is ~28% but expect some overhead for kernel patches and engineering lift. For a rough estimate we'll send a cost table with your current QPS numbers.
[09:58] Arjun Patel: send the cost table please.
[10:01] Maya Chen: we'll attach it.
[10:04] wrap and recap —
[10:05] Maya Chen: recap: agreement on FP8-first rollout, Helix to expand golden prompts to 800 and run tests, Redwood to send configs, runbook, and security addendum. Schedule ops workshop 06/29. Next sync after the ops workshop or earlier if Golden prompt run shows surprises.
[10:25] Nina Lopez: thanks everyone, good meeting.
[10:29] Tom Becker: thanks.
[10:32] Maya Chen: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes and links: shared bench sheet (internal): https://redwood.internal/bench/ff-helix-quant/summary.csv (placeholder)
Security addendum: https://redwood.internal/security/helix-supplement.pdf (placeholder)
Runbook draft: will be attached in follow-up email.

End of transcript.
